messages:
maria_sales: Hey team — POC with NovaHealth hitting weird gaps in traces and a handful of 429s during burst tests. Customer says console shows requests but no trace IDs on their side. Can we swarm?
ingrid_se: thanks for flagging. do you have an example trace id or request id from their logs? also which export target (Splunk/Datadog/S3) are they using?
maria_sales: they tried Splunk HEC first. sample log line they sent: \"level=info service=inference req_id=48f3a2 trace_id=7f3a2b9c-4d2f-11ee-8c99-0242ac120002 error=none\" — but Splunk shows no trace for that id.
raf_engineer: two quick things: 1) ensure we propagate X-Trace-ID (or x-request-id) from front door through the routing layer. 2) 429s likely from per-tenant token bucket — was this a burst test >100rps?
ingrid_se: yep. Maria, can you confirm they set the header key to x-redwood-trace or x-request-id? our sampler looks for either. If not present, we generate a trace but we only export spans when trace sampling hits.
maria_sales: they used x-request-id only. sample header: \"x-request-id: 48f3a2\"
raf_engineer: ok that should be fine. next: ask customer to enable full span export for POC in console (Logs & Traces → Exporters → enable Splunk HEC with debug sampling). I can list the exact steps.
sam_support: copying the quick Splunk HEC fluentd snippet we recommend for POC (customer can run on host or sidecar):
```
<match redwood.logs>
  @type http
  endpoint https://splunk.example.com:8088/services/collector/event/1.0
  headers {"Authorization": "Splunk <HEC_TOKEN>", "Content-Type": "application/json"}
  serializer json
</match>
```
Also make sure HEC index is not dropping events (check quota).
ingrid_se: for console side: Customer -> Observability -> Trace dashboard -> Filter by trace_id=7f3a2b9c... will show if spans reached our exporter queue. If nothing shows, check outgoing egress at the export worker: `/api/v1/exports/splunk/status` (team-internal).
maria_sales: tried the trace dashboard link and it returns empty. they see many requests in the request table but span_count=0.
raf_engineer: that's the smoking gun — we probably didn't attach spans to the request (KV cache warm up path sometimes skips spans for first few tokens). But span_count=0 across many requests suggests exporter suppressed sampling. Can you toggle debug sampling for their org id? Maria I can flip from 0.05 -> 1.0 for 30m to collect everything.
maria_sales: please do, customer is okay.
raf_engineer: done — sampling bumped for org: novahealth -> sampling=1.0 for 30m. deploy-bot: observability-exporter: changed sampling for org novahealth by raf_engineer at 2024-07-05T15:32Z :rocket: :white_check_mark:
sam_support: after sampling bump, ask customer to resend same test and capture one full request/response pair and the headers. if they still don't see the HEC event, collect curl to HEC using the same token to confirm HEC ingestion.
maria_sales: ran the test after bump. they still see 429s at peaks and traces show up intermittently. sample trace id from a successful one: 9c2b11e4-4d33-11ee-8c99-0242ac120002. they attached Splunk raw event and it has body with span data.
ingrid_se: intermittent export + 429s = likely export backlog causing retries. Ask them to check Splunk ingestion latency and our exporter logs for backpressure errors: look for \"exporter_queue_full\" or \"http 503/429 from HEC\".
raf_engineer: also confirm they aren't rate-limiting the HEC token by IP; if HEC returns 429 we backoff and drop spans. We can enable temporary local buffering: set EXPORT_BUFFER_SIZE to 50MB in POC config.
sam_support: sample env patch to apply on their exporter side: 
```
EXPORT_TARGET=splunk
EXPORT_HEC_URL=https://splunk.example.com:8088
EXPORT_HEC_TOKEN=REDACTED
EXPORT_BUFFER_SIZE=52428800
EXPORT_RETRY_BASE_MS=200
```

maria_sales: forwarding all this to NovaHealth ops now. they also asked about billing impact of sampling=1.0 — want a quick estimate.
ingrid_se: explain that trace export doesn't change token billing (tokens charged on inference usage). but storing/exporting spans may incur telemetry cost if they enable retention add-on. for POC we usually absorb telemetry costs for 72h. mention cost estimate link: https://redwood.ai/pricing/telemetry-estimates (internal).
maria_sales: they accepted the POC telemetry absorb for 72h. final ask: can we create a temporary per-org rate bump for request throughput to remove 429s?
raf_engineer: yes — we can create a short-lived higher throughput policy: create policy in routing -> per_org_overrides -> novahealth: max_rps=1200 for 2h. I'll provision now.
raf_engineer: provisioned: novahealth max_rps=1200 until 2024-07-05T18:00Z. monitor and revert after.
maria_sales: customer reran burst tests. 429s dropped to near zero and Splunk shows steady span arrival. they said dashboards are usable now. :tada: thanks everyone.
ingrid_se: follow-up actions: 1) Recommend long-term: enable HEC auto-scale + EXPORT_BUFFER_SIZE 50MB; 2) Add trace header check into onboarding checklist; 3) Add a short KB for POCs about sampling vs billing. I'll own KB.
raf_engineer: I'll add a small guard in exporter to log \"exporter_queue_full\" with org id more prominently so support can triage faster.
sam_support: noted — will send the fluentd snippet + env patch to customer and confirm Splunk ingestion thresholds.
maria_sales: great work. closing loop with NovaHealth. :pray:
